I drew the diagram, saved it as `src-dependencies.png` in the repo root, and opened it in your default image viewer.

What it shows (arrows point from the importing module to the one it imports, labelled with the imported name):

```
app.py ──summary──▶ report.py
report.py ──revenue_series──▶ charts.py
report.py ──monthly_sales──▶ db.py
charts.py ──monthly_sales──▶ db.py
```

- **There are no cycles.** The modules form a clean stack: `app` → `report` → `charts` → `db`.
- **`db.py` is the base layer.** It imports only standard-library modules (`csv`, `pathlib`).
- **`report.py` imports `monthly_sales` from `db` directly,** as well as getting it indirectly through `charts`.

The PNG is untracked, so delete it or add it to `.gitignore` if you don't want it in the repo. The script that draws it is in `/tmp/depdiag/draw.py` if you want to redraw it later.
